items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I mean that ghetto genius that produced Charlie Parker, you know, and Bud Powell and Thelonious Monk now got lost to hip hop

ctx.x: well to get back to my original question, do you have a definition for yourself of a genius in any field?

Well it’s my definition, it won’t conform with the dictionary’s definition, but a genius to me is a person who makes his or her medium different from the way it was before them. You see? And I think a lot of the genius may have gone out of jazz when it became more bourgeois. I mean that ghetto genius that produced Charlie Parker, you know, and Bud Powell and Thelonious Monk now got lost to hip hop because we took the instruments away from the kids. So they made a music out of words. If that genius had gone into…

This is, I’m not sure we can get into this subject at this point, I’ll just throw it out that white musicians often times seem to have more success with a certain style that was created by African-American musicians. Do you think Cecil Taylor was observing the success of people like Dave Brubeck and feeling the unfairness of it?
